cond_0647.intro: We are looking for a Technical System Health Data Scientist to join our team. You will own the development of advanced reports on patient monitoring system usage and system health, working alongside technical experts and customers. These reports will help customers and [Company name masked] understand usage, prevent downtime, and achieve performance SLAs in areas never measured before. You will take ownership of identifying data signatures and sources needed for algorithm development and performance reporting, and lead the development and evaluation of first-of-kind prototypes for IT customers and other relevant partners.
cond_0647.responsibilities:
Determine how customers are using [Company name masked] technology through advanced data analytics on usage, workflow adoption, and outcome achievement:
Defining data flows and schema
Defining technical analytics
Writing scripts and queries
Creating compelling, dynamic data visualizations
Lead collaboration with customers and [Company name masked] experts to advance digital understanding of customer usage and system health of patient monitoring solutions.
Drive reporting on internal performance measures, including asset utilization, service and equipment costs, and volume and revenue to plan that are critical to profitability:
Identify data sources, interfaces and analytics
Define inventory tracking methodology & market inventory management analytics
Identify data sources, interfaces and analytics
Publish customer scorecard internally
Develop new concepts, build proof-of-concept demonstrators, and validate results with customer and field teams.
Direct engagement with business partners and customers to understand their problems, share insights, and validated practices.
Identify gaps and data needs that limit successful measurements of the designed experience.
Lead coordination with other solution and functional teams (e.g., commercial operations, professional services, clinical education, financial administration) to deliver practical and ambitious solutions to these gaps and aspirations.
Determine critical success metrics to gauge the relative performance and progress of managed service customers over time.
